title: Crash reconciliation services
description: Objective: implement safe-boundary drain, release/resume, absent-process recovery, suspect effect handling, and doctor recovery commands. Deliverable: focused runner recovery and daemon recovery modules. NOT in scope: timer-only ownership theft, disaster restore, graph supersession, or optimistic adoption. Hard dependencies: Lease presence core, Projection outbox core, External effect supervisor, Deterministic context journal, and Independent review flow. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/recovery/** and apps/daemon/src/recovery/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: No successor overlaps a predecessor lacking a proven safe release boundary.
Every injected crash yields adopted, absent, suspect, quarantined, or an exact reconciliation command; nothing silently resumes.
Quiet presence alone cannot steal ownership and late observations cannot advance stale authority.
Both focused runner and daemon test commands exit 0.

Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/runner/src/recovery/safe-boundary.ts to green — safe-boundary drain plus release/resume. A successor may overlap a predecessor only when the predecessor's safe release boundary is PROVEN; ACTIVE and UNKNOWN both block, with distinct codes. Drain is monotonic: a drain disposition may be upgraded by a later reason but never downgraded, and an attempted downgrade is a refusal rather than a silent no-op, so a weaker later signal cannot walk back a stronger earlier one. Every fact is caller-supplied — lease epoch and token from the lease core, effect status as a classification, process exit as the imported ClaudeProcessExit. There is no clock and no randomness in this module: no Date.now, no Math.random, no elapsed-time reasoning of any kind, which is also what makes DoD 3's timer-based ownership theft unwritable. Target under 250 lines.

Created packages/runner/src/recovery/safe-boundary.ts (230 lines, under the 250 target).

- admitSuccessorOverlap: PROVEN_RELEASED is the ONLY admitting value and is tested by positive equality, so a later member added to the lattice blocks by default instead of falling through to an admission. ACTIVE and UNKNOWN block under distinct codes.
- admitResume: admissible only when the boundary is PROVEN_RELEASED **and** carries its exact safe handoff; anything else refuses RECOVERY_RESUME_BOUNDARY_UNPROVEN rather than resuming from whatever is on disk.
- advanceRecoveryDrain: the two recovery-layer rules a crash makes possible — a DROPPED held reason and a WALKED-BACK strongest reason — are refusals under their own codes, never a silent no-op returning the held disposition. The union itself is DELEGATED to the supervisor's upgradeDisposition (the single declared source of drain monotonicity); nothing is re-derived here. Any other self-inconsistency is refused BY that source and carried through verbatim via carriedFailure, so the DRAIN layer stays visible in the failure.
  Ordering note, deliberate: the recovery downgrade/drop checks run BEFORE the observed disposition's isMonotonicDisposition check. Both orders refuse, but this order gives the specific, actionable diagnosis ("a reason was walked back") instead of the generic "not monotonic", and it keeps RECOVERY_DRAIN_DOWNGRADE_REFUSED reachable — under the reverse order the supervisor would always answer first and that code could never be produced, which is the vacuous-refusal shape epic rail 6 warns about.
- Ingress uses the supervisor's exactRecord/isRef/oneOf, so accessor and prototype smuggling are refused by the same hardened readers the rest of the package uses; no parser is cloned.
- Clock/randomness/process fence verified now, not deferred: `grep -rn "Date\.now|Math\.random|child_process|spawn|kill("` over packages/runner/src/recovery/ returns ZERO hits. The module doc comment was reworded so it does not name those APIs literally — a comment spelling one out trips the grep exactly like a call would, and step 8 needs the sweep to mean what it says.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/runner/src/recovery/crash-classification.ts to green — absent-process recovery and suspect effect handling. Given durable records plus a caller-supplied crash observation, classify into exactly one of the five closed outcome kinds. The rules that matter: an effect whose status cannot be established is SUSPECT, never optimistically adopted, and a SUSPECT effect is never auto-resumed; a process proven absent with all resources proven released is ABSENT; anything with an unreconciled resource is QUARANTINED with what remains held named explicitly; and where no local decision is safe, emit an exact RECONCILIATION_COMMAND describing precisely what an operator or adapter must do, rather than guessing. Ownership transfer requires a proven epoch or token advance from the lease core — quiescence is never authority. A stale-epoch observation is refused, never merged. Import ClaudeProcessExit and the reconciled-outcome vocabulary from providers/claude rather than restating them. Target under 250 lines.

Created packages/runner/src/recovery/crash-classification.ts (209 lines).

Design: the classifier RE-DERIVES NOTHING the supervisor already owns. reconstructAfterRestart carries the 786/787 table and the ambiguity rules; this layer adds only the two questions recovery itself must answer — may ownership move, and may a late observation speak.

Classification order IS the safety order, and each ordering choice is load-bearing:
- SUSPECT before adoption, so an UNESTABLISHED effect is never optimistically adopted and never auto-resumed, even under a fully advanced fence.
- Quarantine before absence, so a run still holding a resource or a proven-active effect can never be reported as gone.
- ABSENT requires a POSITIVE death observation: processExit.kind !== "UNOBSERVED", plus PROVEN_ABSENT effect status and a terminal/tombstoned post state. Not seeing life is not seeing death; an UNOBSERVED exit falls through to a reconciliation command instead.
- QUARANTINED names what remains held as explicit strings ("resource:UNKNOWN", "effect:<ref>"), not a count or a boolean.
- The fallthrough emits an EXACT command typed as RuntimeCommandKind from @moe/contracts ("recovery.inspect_external" for records no local decision can settle, "recovery.reconcile_external" otherwise) — a typo is a type error rather than a bad instruction to an operator.

DoD 3, ownershipProven(): requires the claimed authority's epoch to be STRICTLY GREATER than the durable lease epoch AND its token to differ from the held one. A proof at the held epoch is the crashed process's own authority replayed. `presenceLooksLive` is parsed and validated but is CONSULTED NOWHERE in the decision — the only durable way to keep "quiet presence is not authority" true is to leave it no place to be read.

Two deliberate rejections recorded for review:
- An earlier draft exported RECOVERY_PROPOSED_COMMANDS built with `.filter(kind => RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.includes(kind))`. Removed: a filter fails OPEN — a command that drifted out of the vocabulary would silently vanish from the list and the export would still look healthy. The `RuntimeCommandKind` type annotation already fails the build on drift, which is the fail-closed form.
- CLAUDE_RECONCILED_OUTCOMES is deliberately NOT imported here despite the step text. Binding a provider-specific outcome list into a provider-neutral classifier would be the wrong seam; the durable records carry the neutral SettlementEvidence.outcomeClass, and the provider-owned ClaudeProcessExit type IS imported and used in provenAbsent(). The test suite does pin CLAUDE_RECONCILIATION_VERSION in its fixture.

Test correction made while going green: the "reaches ABSENT once the effect is proven absent" case had `attempt: makeAttempt({state:"LAUNCH_REQUESTED"})` against `attemptState:"ABSENT"`, which recordsDisagree refuses — so the case was exercising the incoherent-records path while asserting only `not.toBe("SUSPECT")`, which would have passed for the wrong reason. Now `attempt: null` and the assertion is the exact `toBe("ABSENT")`.

Created apps/daemon/src/recovery/doctor-commands.ts (217 lines) and its suite (205 lines). No package.json or lock change — step 1 established the daemon half needs only @moe/contracts, which it already declares.

Ingress follows apps/daemon/src/index.ts exactly: decodeBoundedJsonBytes, then an exact-shape check against a frozen key list plus the pinned schemaVersion literal, then compose, returning a frozen discriminated union.

Report-and-propose is enforced STRUCTURALLY, not by a check:
- The only success shapes are REPORTED and PROPOSED; both carry `appliesChange: false` and every proposal carries `confirmationRequired: true`. A repair-without-confirmation command would have to add a new arm to the union rather than slip through an existing one.
- Proposals are looked up in a frozen kind→RuntimeCommandKind map rather than derived from the kind's NAME, so a kind with no declared runtime operation reports instead of inventing an operation to propose.

Assertions, all pinning code AND layer:
- Command surface asserted by SET EQUALITY against a hand-transcribed five-member list, plus a second rule-level assertion that every kind begins with `doctor.report_` or `doctor.propose_` — so a repair command cannot appear even under an innocuous name — plus a non-zero cardinality guard so the loop cannot pass vacuously.
- Every declared kind is executed and asserted to leave appliesChange false; the proposal subset is asserted to have exactly PROPOSALS.length members, so a proposal silently degrading to a report is caught.
- Two-layer refusals kept distinct: a non-bytes payload and malformed JSON refuse at BOUNDED_JSON with the decoder's own codes (JSON_INPUT_TYPE_INVALID, JSON_SYNTAX_INVALID); extra key, missing key, wrong schemaVersion, undeclared kind (`doctor.apply_recovery`) and a negative epoch all refuse DOCTOR_REQUEST_SHAPE_INVALID@DOCTOR; a behind-record observedEpoch refuses DOCTOR_AUTHORITY_STALE@DOCTOR.
- Ordering pinned explicitly: a request that is BOTH malformed and stale must answer with the SHAPE refusal, so a shape check that started letting malformed input reach the epoch comparison shows up as a red test rather than staying green on "it refused".
- Positive controls included (equal epoch and beyond-record epoch both admit), so the stale-authority refusal is not vacuously refusing everything.

Each file was backed up OUT OF TREE (C:/Users/.../Temp/moe-drill-52ec) and every restore was verified by git hash-object against the pre-drill hash; all 24 restores printed restored-ok.

- M1 UNKNOWN-blocks-successor (=== "PROVEN_RELEASED" -> !== "ACTIVE") KILLED, 2 failed/50 passed: "blocks a successor over a predecessor whose release cannot be established" + the lattice sweep. DoD 1's optimistic-implementation arm is genuinely covered.

- M5 EPOCH-ADVANCE REQUIREMENT (claimed.epoch > held.epoch -> true) KILLED, 1 failed: "refuses to adopt on an authority whose epoch never advanced". This was the one to watch — DoD 3's ownership-theft protection is demonstrably tested, not merely present.

No input can redden it. Attack questions from the step, each answered against the code:
- Can a successor start while a predecessor's release is merely unproven? No. admitSuccessorOverlap admits ONLY on positive equality with PROVEN_RELEASED, so a member added to the lattice later blocks by default. Drilled: flipping it to `!== "ACTIVE"` reddens the named UNKNOWN test.
- Can quiet presence, elapsed time, or a retry count transfer ownership anywhere? No. presenceLooksLive is parsed and validated but read NOWHERE in any decision. There is no clock, no counter that grows while nothing happens, and no elapsed-time quantity in scope; the extended fence grep (child_process, spawn(, kill(, Date.now, Math.random, new Date(, performance.now, setTimeout, hrtime) is zero over both owned directories.
- Can a late observation advance authority? No — refused with RECOVERY_STALE_OBSERVATION_REFUSED, and a separate test asserts the refused kind is outside RECOVERY_OUTCOME_KINDS so "refused" cannot degrade into "silently dropped".
- Any path that resumes without an explicit outcome kind? No. The classifier has no RESUMED arm; admitResume demands a proven boundary carrying its exact handoff; the daemon's doctor.propose_resume proposes work.resume for confirmation and never applies it.
- Can a drain disposition be downgraded? No — dropped-reason and walked-back-strongest each refuse under their own code, and a retargeted record is refused by the supervisor's single monotonicity source with its layer preserved.
- Does a doctor command apply a repair without confirmation? Structurally impossible: the only success arms are REPORTED and PROPOSED, both carry appliesChange:false, every proposal carries confirmationRequired:true, and the kind list is asserted by set equality plus a naming rule.
- Is any unbuilt module's shape guessed at? No. Journal and review-package digests are opaque 64-hex references validated for shape only and never interpreted; effect identity is an opaque ref. Neither the context journal nor the review flow is imported.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) WHY THIS IS NOT BLOCKED, though the promotion note called it the deep end and expected report_blocked. All three unbuilt dependencies enter this task as OBSERVATIONS AND IDENTITIES, never as calls. The whole runner subtree is already fenced so that OS and process facts arrive as caller-supplied observations — the Claude adapter and the supervisor both work this way — and crash reconciliation is the purest case of it: a crash is by definition something you learn about after the fact from durable records plus an observation. So: effect identity is an opaque reference; the effect's own SUSPECT/absent/active status is a caller-supplied classification, not something this module asks the supervisor for; journal and review artifacts are cited by content-addressed digest. Nothing here imports an unbuilt module, so nothing here is speculative. Both owned directories are greenfield, so nothing collides either.
(2) DoD 2 IS AN OUTCOME-SET PROPERTY, so it drives the design. 'Every injected crash yields adopted, absent, suspect, quarantined, or an exact reconciliation command; nothing silently resumes' means the classifier's outcome kinds are a CLOSED exported list and the test asserts SET EQUALITY against it. That is what makes 'nothing silently resumes' checkable rather than aspirational — a sixth outcome, or a silent resume, shows up as a set mismatch instead of hiding.
(3) THE DAEMON HALF MAY NEED A PACKAGE EDGE. apps/daemon depends only on @moe/contracts and @moe/scheduler; doctor recovery commands will likely need @moe/runner and/or @moe/store. (4) SPLIT BY PACKAGE, NOT BY CONCERN. The runner half is pure classification and boundary logic; the daemon half is command ingress. Keeping them apart matches the two owned path roots and the two-command verification gate.

planningNotes.risks:
1. **DoD 3 is the security-shaped one: 'quiet presence alone cannot steal ownership'.** The failure mode is a recovery path that treats 'the process seems to be alive' or 'nobody has objected for a while' as authority to take over. Ownership transfer must require a proven fence — epoch or token advance from the lease core — never quiescence and never elapsed time. There is no clock in this subtree at all (no Date.now), which makes timer-based theft unwritable; keep it that way and assert the refusal code for the nearest legal attempt.
2. **'Late observations cannot advance stale authority'** needs its own fixture: an observation carrying an older epoch than the durable record must be REFUSED with a stable code, not merged, not ignored silently. Ignoring it silently would pass a weak test while losing the refusal the DoD asks for — assert the code, not just the absence of a change.
3. **DoD 1's overlap rule is the one that corrupts data if wrong.** A successor may only start when the predecessor has a PROVEN safe release boundary; unknown release status must block the successor, not allow it. Test all three predecessor states — proven released, proven active, and UNKNOWN — and assert UNKNOWN blocks, since that is the arm an optimistic implementation gets wrong.
4. **DoD 2 must be asserted as SET EQUALITY** over the closed outcome list, with per-kind counts recorded so a sweep that only ever produces one kind is visible. Assert the generated case count is non-zero (epic rail 6) — a crash sweep that injects zero crashes passes while testing nothing.
5. Effect identity, journal digests and review-package digests are opaque content-addressed references validated for shape only. The modules that own them are unbuilt; inventing their internals here creates a seam that must later be undone.
6. The daemon amendment may already be landed by a sibling. Check before requesting, keep any lock change to the single hunk, and verify with `git diff --stat pnpm-lock.yaml`.
7. Two gates must BOTH exit 0 (`@moe/runner` and `@moe/daemon`). A change on one side can redden the other; run both before claiming completion.
8. Known flake, not yours: the `scope-observation` real-git test can hit a 5s timeout. Re-run once, report, do not chase.
